verdict.rationale: pnpm is documented as a drop-in replacement for npm that works on any existing project. It installs from and verifies signatures against the registries it pulls from, and it publishes to the remote registry, so it plugs into the npm registry ecosystem. Community users also report it working in large real-world projects. However, the docs only imply which registry it uses rather than describing it, and some dependencies needed workarounds such as --shamefully-hoist. Missing for 10: explicit documentation naming the npm registry and its scale or maintenance, and explicit coverage of alternative registry sources (private registries, git, or tarball installs).
